name: Marketing agency hero: headline text clipped to an inverted-color window of the background photo
notes: The signature move: two of the three headline words are set with background-image: the same hero photo, background-clip:text, then filter:invert(1) contrast(1.25) brightness(1.15) — so each letter reads as a bright inverted-color 'window' cut into the same dark photo behind it, no image editing required. The clipped words use background-attachment:fixed so their crop lines up with the viewport rather than just the text's own bounding box (falls back to background-attachment:scroll under 720px where fixed backgrounds misbehave on mobile Safari). Keep the third line (.plain) as solid paper-white — an all-masked headline reads muddy; the contrast between one plain line and two masked lines is what sells the effect. Swap the background-image url in both .hero-bg and .mask-heading span together or the mask stops matching the base photo.
